sources.used_for: Rounded 'Say' dimensions: 7.4 ft span, 3.7 ft wrist span, 4 in shoulder span, 8 in maximum body width and 55 in overall length; the paragraph supplies total wing area 6.61 ft^2. The illustrated outline informs the parallel-chord inner and tapered outer panels.
Qualitative distinction between arm/inner and hand/outer wing panels, and the proposal for a conventional tail, fin and rudder.

assumptions: Conversions use exactly 1 ft = 0.3048 m and 1 in = 0.0254 m; aspect ratio is derived as span squared divided by area (about 8.284), consistent with the page's rounded 8.29.
Individual wing length is (span - shoulder span)/2, rather than the excluded printed wing-length entry.
The animated visual uses an assumed sinusoidal 18 degree inner stroke and an additional 28 degree outer-panel stroke at the specified 2 Hz powered phase; these angles are visual articulation only.
Mass, gravity, density, force polar, powered-drive efficiency, controls and contact rules are the task's new benchmark assumptions, not claims made by Stanley J. O. Tinn.
excluded_fields: Page 14 biological stroke-angle reference frames, elastic stiffness, vortex-lift landing hypothesis and unspecified curved-plate polar.
Any Standard Model Swan or earlier human-carrying simulator data.
limitations: Historical photographs are design notes and observations, not a complete or validated blueprint.
This is a cycle-averaged point-mass educational model with independently animated panels, not a structural, unsteady-flow or aeroelastic solver.
Powered thrust is an assumed flapping drive represented by a power model and is not experimentally proven wing performance.
Tail and fin geometry is a clear qualitative visualization; exact shape, section and control effectiveness are not specified by the sources.
